name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
summary: Cholera has killed about 1,800 in DR Congo this year, including the conflict-hit east, as Ebola spreads
state: WHO reported in early November that cholera has killed about 1,800 people in DR Congo in 2026, from about 60,000 cases, a fatality rate near 3% (AFP via Medical Xpress, 5 Nov). MSF is responding to a severe epidemic in Sangé, South Kivu, a conflict-affected province, and UN agencies say cases spiked in October as the country also fights Ebola (MSF; UN News). This meets the Alert line for a large, high-mortality outbreak in a conflict zone.
for_you: Travellers to DR Congo should check FCDO travel advice and NaTHNaC health guidance. Displaced families in eastern DR Congo, with poor access to clean water and care, face the highest risk.
rubric_hit: Large high-mortality outbreak in a conflict zone: DRC cholera ~1,800 deaths, ~60,000 cases in 2026 (Alert)

why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
